This section organizes the shared concepts behind CNC routers and mills. The exact machine, controller, tooling, material, and classroom activity may differ.

## Learning sequence

- CNC router and CNC mill capabilities and limits;
- machine coordinates, work coordinates, and zero/reference choices;
- secure workholding and clearance planning;
- end-mill geometry and tool selection;
- CAM setup, pockets, profiles, drilling, and toolpath order;
- feeds, speeds, chip formation, and machine/material-specific evidence;
- simulation, dry-run practices, verification, inspection, and revision.

Machine-specific safety instruction follows school board guidelines and the course information provided by the teacher. Students in Mr. Andrade's classes use Google Classroom for that material.

## Free background resources

Explore parametric parts and CAM concepts with [FreeCAD](https://www.freecad.org/), open machine-control documentation through [LinuxCNC](https://linuxcnc.org/) and the [official GRBL repository](https://github.com/gnea/grbl), and structured CAD/CAM instruction through [Autodesk Fusion learning](https://help.autodesk.com/view/fusion360/ENU/courses/). Generic feeds and speeds remain starting hypotheses until they are verified for the machine, tool, material, workholding, and required finish. See the [full free-resource directory · Work in Progress](../resources/work-in-progress/index.qmd) for additional design, inspection, and fabrication references.

::: {.ter-curriculum-relevance}
**Ontario curriculum relevance:** Strongest fit with **TMJ Manufacturing Technology**, **TDJ Technological Design**, and **TCJ Construction Technology**, including relevant senior-course contexts involving CAM, machining, mechanical engineering, and manufacturing.

Potential senior contexts include **TMJ3M/TMJ4M**, **TMJ3C/TMJ4C**, **TMJ3E/TMJ4E**, **TDJ3M/TDJ4M**, and **TDJ3O/TDJ4O**. Course codes identify useful contexts, not one-to-one expectation mappings.
:::

For currently supported digital fabrication, use [Laser Cutting & 2D Fabrication](../03-laser-cutting/index.qmd) or [3D Printing](../04-3d-printing/index.qmd).
